findings.description: The spike says "New decision 208 (the next free number)", but docs/adr/0208-three-architecture-review-candidates-are-set-aside.md already exists, and the latest decision is 208, so the next free number is 209.
findings.body:
**Decision 208 is already taken.** The spike says `New decision 208 (the next free number) carries the pipeline`, and line 494 repeats `decision 208`. But [`docs/adr/0208-three-architecture-review-candidates-are-set-aside.md`](https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/pupitre/blob/763843807579b400ca3ee74fb19d87f048527d87/docs/adr/0208-three-architecture-review-candidates-are-set-aside.md) was accepted just before this spike (commits b5847fa5, d6ba49d1), and nothing in `docs/adr/` is numbered above it, so the next free number is 209.

The follow-up task that writes the ADR would collide with the existing 208, and every `decision 208` reference in this spike would point at the architecture-review decision. Change both mentions to 209:

- https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/pupitre/blob/763843807579b400ca3ee74fb19d87f048527d87/docs/spikes/2026-11-23-ticket-pipeline.md#L359-L359
- https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/pupitre/blob/763843807579b400ca3ee74fb19d87f048527d87/docs/spikes/2026-11-23-ticket-pipeline.md#L494-L494 (`After task 7, the 187 and 176 amendments and decision 209 are written in`)

findings.description: Task 7's scope-in lists src/core/session-repository.ts, but the real file is src/core/session.repository.ts.
findings.body:
**Task 7 scopes a file that does not exist.** The scope-in lists `src/core/session-repository.ts`. The real file is [`src/core/session.repository.ts`](https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/pupitre/blob/763843807579b400ca3ee74fb19d87f048527d87/src/core/session.repository.ts#L91), which uses the `kebab-case.role.ts` naming. Its `insertTask` is the function that writes tasks, so it is the file `pup plan from-ticket` needs.

The spike presents its slices as ready for `pup plan add`, and scope-in becomes the scope hook's allowlist. A worker planned from this glob would be blocked from editing the repository it has to change.

The test glob on the same line, `test/core/ticket-plan*.test.ts`, has the separate `test/unit/` problem noted in the nits below.

https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/pupitre/blob/763843807579b400ca3ee74fb19d87f048527d87/docs/spikes/2026-11-23-ticket-pipeline.md#L482-L483

findings.description: The slice plan's test scope-in globs use test/core/... (and dotted names such as design-note.utils.test.ts), but docs/conventions/naming.md puts tests under test/unit/<path> with the dash form, so planned tasks would scope-block their own tests.

The label table says pup removes `specified` on a rejection or an approval, but T9 says nothing is written until T11 and the rejection section has the operator remove `specified` by hand; the spike contradicts itself on who removes it.
The spike and task 1 call for a `retryable` TrackerUnavailableError, but the class in src/core/errors/tracker.errors.ts has `rateLimited` and no `retryable` field.
Tasks 3 and 4 scope `src/core/migrations/**`, which does not exist; the schema lives in src/core/db.client.ts, which neither task lists, so the worker cannot touch the real schema file.
The specifier session is launched with no task, but decision 40 makes sessions.task_id NOT NULL; the spike should give it a synthetic task or list decision 40 among the amended decisions.

Rejection-reason comments are trusted on authorAssociation OWNER/MEMBER/COLLABORATOR, which does not imply write access, unlike the `ready` gate's admin/write permission check; use the same permission check or the tickets.operator login.

Defaulting tickets.operator to the repo owner fails on an org-owned repo, since an org never appears as a label event's User actor, so every design-approved would be removed; default to the `gh api user` login instead.

T1 refuses to comment to a labeller without write access, but T9 comments to anyone but the operator who applies design-approved, which triage-level users can do; make T9 silent for labellers without write access.

The rate-limit estimate is off: three `gh issue list` calls per 60 s is about 180 an hour, not about 60. They go over GraphQL with a permission call per issue, and the updatedAt skip needs a field Tracker.listReady does not return, which task 1 does not add.
